description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.

summary.one_liner: Ponytail is a prompt-based skill that makes AI coding agents write the minimal code a task needs, with commands for reviewing diffs, auditing repos, and tracking deferred shortcuts.
summary.what_it_does: The repo ships one prompt, skills/ponytail/SKILL.md, plus a compact AGENTS.md for agents that read rules files, and adapters that load this prompt into different agents. The prompt tells the agent to understand the problem and read the code a change touches first, then choose the smallest solution that still handles validation, error handling, security and accessibility. In Claude Code and Codex it adds slash commands: /ponytail to set an intensity level, /ponytail-review to review the current diff or a PR, /ponytail-audit to check the whole repo, /ponytail-debt to collect deferred shortcut comments into a ledger, /ponytail-gain to show benchmark results, and /ponytail-help. In Claude Code, a band above the prompt shows per-task cost, tokens, agent time, reuse of existing code and test status, and a local Board page stores session history under ~/.config/ponytail/band/. The README reports its own benchmark (39 tasks, Opus 5.5, 5 runs each) claiming about 53% less code and 41% less time than the same agent without the skill; these figures are the author's and are documented in a linked results file.
use_cases: Keep an AI coding agent from over-engineering small features
Review a diff or PR for bugs, security and missing tests
Audit a whole repository and rank what to fix first
Track deliberate shortcuts left as comments
Reduce token cost and agent time of coding sessions
Add a lightweight rules file to Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf or Cline
how_to_run: Copy AGENTS.md into your project (any other agent), or ask your agent to install skills/ponytail/SKILL.md as a skill; see INSTALL.md
notable: Single prompt file (skills/ponytail/SKILL.md) reused across many agent hosts via adapters
Review and audit commands that trace the code a change touches, not just the diff, and explain what goes wrong and what happens if unfixed
Shortcut comments tracked into a ledger with /ponytail-debt
Claude Code band and local Board page showing per-task cost, tokens and test status
Explicit rule that security, validation, error handling and accessibility are never cut
caveats: The band requires Claude Code 2.1.290 or later and does not show in the VS Code chat panel, cloud sessions or claude -p
Slash commands need a skill-capable host; Cursor rule files, Windsurf, Cline, Copilot and Kiro get only the always-on ruleset without commands
Benchmark numbers are self-reported by the author on a specific setup (Opus 5.5, 39 tasks)
